title: The impact of hydrothermal synthesis parameters on the biological activities and structural characteristics of carbon quantum dots synthesized from citrus peel
content: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have emerged as a promising nanomaterial due to their superior antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. This study successfully synthesized CQDs from citrus peels by a hydrothermal method at a temperature of 200 °C for 5 hours with a content of 0.4 g L−1 at a pH value of 3. Under the optimized conditions, the synthesized carbon quantum dots (CQDs) exhibited an oxidation resistance of 90–100%, as validated by ABTS and DPPH assays. Furthermore, these CQDs displayed potent antimicrobial activity, effectively inhibiting and neutralizing E. coli and S. aureus over a 24 hours period. Structural characterization utilizing the Debye–Scherrer formula indicated crystallite sizes ranging from 2.72 nm (pomelo) to 8.28 nm (kumquat), while lemon and orange peel-derived samples yielded sizes of 5.43 nm and 4.05 nm, respectively. Morphological analysis revealed spherical structures with particle diameters below 10 nm, characterized by the presence of C═  O, C–N, and –OH functional groups. These results underscore the significant potential of citrus peel-derived CQDs for multifaceted applications in biomedicine, food technology, and related disciplines.
